excerpts.locator: Handbook 2026/27 PDF p.125 (printed pp.241-242), Rule M.1
excerpts.paraphrase: Before each season a club gives every first-team squad member a different shirt number.
A player joining the first-team squad mid-season is also given a shirt number.
Unless the Board consents in writing, numbers begin at one and run consecutively.
A player keeps his allocated number for the whole season while he stays with the club.
When a player leaves, his number may be given to someone else.
In league matches the shirt back shows the player number clearly, with his surname above it.
The number also appears on the front of one leg of the shorts.
The goalkeeper shirt and socks must differ from outfield players and match officials; the rule concerns kit, not a number.

excerpts.locator: Wikipedia Squad number, History, First use of numbers
excerpts.paraphrase: English league clubs wore numbers by field position on 25 August 1928; earlier uses existed in Australia and Argentina.
The Football League made numbered shirts compulsory from the 1939-40 season.
In 1993 the FA moved to persistent squad numbers instead of 1-11 for the starting line-up.
England traditional 4-4-2: 2 and 3 full-backs, 5 and 6 centre-backs, 4 defensive midfielder.
Argentina 4-3-3 list: number 5 is the central defensive midfielder.
Argentina 4-3-3 list: number 6 is the second centre-back or stopper.
Brazil list: number 5 is the first volante, a defensive midfielder.

excerpts.locator: Wikipedia Squad number, Unusual or notable numbers
excerpts.paraphrase: At the 1958 World Cup numbers were handed out at random after Brazil omitted its list; Pele was given the 10.
